sentences.text: Saurophaganax is a dubious and chimeric genus of large saurischian dinosaur that may have been a sauropod.
Currently, the genus is classified as incertae sedis, meaning its family placement remains uncertain.
The name combines Greek words for lizard and eat with a Latin term meaning the largest.
The holotype, the specimen the species is based on, is a single neural arch.
John Willis Stovall discovered remains of a large dinosaur near Kenton in Cimarron County, Oklahoma, in the latest Kimmeridgian layers.
In 1941, Stovall named the remains Saurophagus maximus in an article by journalist Grace Ernestine Ray.
In 1995, Daniel Chure established the new genus Saurophaganax by adding the Greek suffix meaning ruler to the previous name.
In 1987, Spencer George Lucas incorrectly designated a tibia as the lectotype without realizing the genus was invalid.
Very little is known about the behavior of Saurophaganax due to the rarity of its fossil remains.
The taxonomic placement of Saurophaganax is unstable, with studies suggesting it could be related to Metriacanthosauridae, Allosauria, or Carcharodontosauria.
A 2024 reassessment suggested that the allosaurid specimens previously assigned to Saurophaganax belong to a new species of Allosaurus named Allosaurus anax.
The type species of the genus Saurophaganax is Saurophaganax maximus.
Saurophaganax lived in the Late Jurassic, specifically within the Kimmeridgian stage of the Morrison Formation, which dates from approximately 156.3 to 146.8 million years ago.
The Morrison Basin, where Saurophaganax fossils were found, stretched from New Mexico to Alberta and Saskatchewan.
The environment where Saurophaganax lived was a semiarid region with distinct wet and dry seasons.

Researchers suggested that the holotype could not be confidently identified as a theropod or sauropod, although complex accessory laminae are more comparable to sauropods, especially juvenile Apatosaurus specimens.
Some referred specimens likely belong to diplodocids rather than the large allosaurid from the Kenton 1 quarry.
